strings: Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
A snack machine courtesy of the Getmore Chocolate Corporation, based out of Mars.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
Contains pills used to treat genetic abnormalities.
Drymate brand monkey cubes. Just add water!
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
The cornerstone of any customer service job. You feel an unending urge to ring it.
A tank full of industrial welding fuel. Do not consume.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
These may, or may not, grow into wheat.
Boil 'em! Mash 'em! Stick 'em in a stew!
These seeds grow into apple trees.
A reminder of meals gone by.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
Bluespace technologies on the application of bureaucracy.
A compact medical bed. This emergency version can be folded and carried for quick transport.
A dorky fannypack for keeping small items in. Concealed enough, or ugly enough to avert their eyes, that others won't see what you put in or take out easily.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
A simple yet bulky storage device for gas tanks.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
A covered turret that shoots at its enemies.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images. This one will refuse to auto-connect incoming calls.
A high-capacity superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit.
Used to control a room's automated defenses.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A remotely-activatable dispenser for crowd-controlling foam.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
Magnetic boots, often used during extravehicular activity to ensure the user remains safely attached to the vehicle.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
A powerful and versatile flashbulb device, with applications ranging from disorienting attackers to acting as visual receptors in robot production.
The Warrior's bland acronym, MMI, obscures the true horror of this monstrosity, that nevertheless has become standard-issue on Nanotrasen stations.
Used for scanning and alerting when someone enters a certain proximity.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with generic programs.
Used to access the station's automated alert system.
It monitors power levels across the station.
Used to monitor the station's air alarms.
A charging dock for energy based weaponry, PDAs, and other devices.
An intercom primarily used for a private line directly to the station's AI.
It's a normal black ink pen.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A wall with rough iron plating.
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
A wall-mounted first aid station, designed to treat minor injuries - just stick your hand in and try to relax.

An industrial unit made to hold, charge, and decontaminate equipment. It comes with a built-in UV cauterization mechanism. A small warning label advises that organic matter should not be placed into the unit.
It's used for removing weeds or scratching your back.
The Human Harvest: From Seed to Market
Crack it open, inhale the musk of its pages, and learn something new.
A scanner used to evaluate a plant's various areas of growth, genetic traits and chemicals.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
A basin used to grow plants in.
A small tool for digging and moving dirt.
A special pipe to bridge pipe layers with.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
A sign labelling an area where exodrones are used.
Just looking at this thing makes you feel tired.
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
It has some unsavory stains on it...
A beacon used by a teleporter.
Contains all the luck you'll ever need.
A portable flashing device. Wrench to activate and deactivate. Cannot detect slow movements.
A large vessel containing pressurized gas.
A wrench with common uses. Can be found in your hand.
Used for emergencies. Contains very little oxygen, so try to conserve it until you actually need it.
A small crowbar. This handy tool is useful for lots of things, such as prying floor tiles or opening unpowered doors.
A face-covering mask that can be connected to an air supply. Good for concealing your identity and with a filter slot to help remove those toxins.
It's the hub of a teleporting machine.
A sign labelling the AI's heavily-fortified satellite.
It's Officer Beepsky! Powered by a potato and a shot of whiskey, and with a sturdier reinforced chassis, too.
This device recharges energy-dependent lifeforms, like cyborgs, ethereals, and MODsuit users.
Used for pulsing wires to test which to cut. Not recommended by doctors. You can activate it in-hand to locate the nearest APC.
A sign labelling an area where the station's radio and NTnet servers are stored.
The power control station for a bluespace teleporter. Used for toggling power, and can activate a test-fire to prevent malfunctions.
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
A flexible, superconducting insulated multilayer hub for heavy-duty multilayer power transfer.
The lynchpin of a GOOD transit system.
Use this to keep prisoners in line.
The latest and greatest power razor born from the science of shaving.
Used to control a linked teleportation Hub and Station.
A transit tube for moving things around.
A warning sign which reads 'EXTERNAL AIRLOCK'.
A full tile window that is reinforced with metal rods.
A station intercom. It looks like it has been modified to not broadcast.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
This is used to lie in, sleep in or strap on.
Pstttthhh! Pass it under the table.
An old, deactivated cyborg. Whilst once actively used to guard against intruders, it now simply intimidates them with its cold, steely gaze.
A suit that completely restrains the wearer. Manufactured by Antyphun Corp.
A tank with an N2O/O2 gas mix.
A close-fitting sterile mask that can be connected to an air supply.
A remote control switch for a mounted flasher.
A remote control switch for a mounted igniter.
A desk lamp with an adjustable mount.
A tool used by great men to placate the frothing masses. Can be used to hasten allies with right-click.
The Secure Apprehension Device, as developed by Nanotrasen. Delivers a precise shock to a target's central nervous system to incapacitate them.
WARNING: These devices are extremely dangerous and can cause blindness or deafness in repeated use.
It's a storage unit for level 3 biohazard gear.
A large duffel bag for holding extra supplies - this one has a material inlay with space for various sharp-looking tools.

It's a bucket with a sensor attached.
A sign labelling an area where scientific data is stored.
A pole with powerful mounted lights on it. Due to its high power draw, it must be powered by a direct connection to a wire node.

A massive module rack which can hold many modules including a core law module. 		It can even be linked to other module racks to add additional slots. 		Designed to be used by the station's primary AI and its legion of cyborgs.

One of the more successful achievements of the Nanotrasen Corporate Warfare Division, their nuclear fission explosives are renowned for being cheap to produce and devastatingly effective. Signs explain that though this particular device has been decommissioned, every Nanotrasen station is equipped with an equivalent one, just in case. All Captains carefully guard the disk needed to detonate them - at least, the sign says they do. There seems to be a tap on the back.
A state of the art medical device that can restore someone's physical appearance to the last known DNA database backup.
box of shotgun shells (Less Lethal - Beanbag)
A box full of beanbag shotgun shells, designed for shotguns.
A strangely translucent and iridescent crystal.
A comfy-looking dog bed. You can even strap your pet in, in case the gravity turns off.
It's got ELECTROLYTES! Only to be consumed in the freedom of a dispenser zone. The punch zone is practiced without conflicting with institutional policies, public safety, or daily operations.
A weak beanbag slug for riot control.
It's an industrial strength book scanner. Perfect!
A poster encouraging you to work for your future.
A stuffed toy that resembles a syndicate nuclear operative. The tag claims operatives to be purely fictitious.
A generic floppy disk. No way Nanotrasen still uses those, right?
Use this if your friends left you behind.
A not so comfortable looking bed with some nozzles at the top and bottom. It will keep someone in stasis.
A crudely-made sign with the words 'fok of' written in some sort of red paint.
Several lumps of snow put together to form a snowman.

The command's special free-frequency intercom. It's a versatile tool that can be tuned to any frequency, granting you access to channels you're not supposed to be on. Plus, it comes equipped with a built-in voice amplifier for crystal-clear communication.
Talk through this... to confess your many sins. Conceals your voice, to keep them secret.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with research programs.
For the bulkier art pieces, hand-picked by the curator.
A sign reminding you to remain behind the firing line, and to wear ear protection.
It's a watering can. It is scientifically proved that using a watering can to simulate rain increases plant happiness!
A robust satchel for stashing your loot.
This little bugger can be used to store and transport ores.
A slithery snake. These legless reptiles are the bane of mice and adventurers alike.
A first aid kit for when you get toolboxed.
A crate containing an assortment of cheap prosthetic limbs.
A specially formed bowl of ancient design. It is possible to crush or juice items placed in it using a pestle; however the process, unlike modern methods, is slow and physically exhausting.
An ancient, simple tool used in conjunction with a mortar to grind or juice items.
It's a baseball hat in a tasteless black colour.
A standard black and white striped uniform to signal authority.
A police whistle for when you need to make sure the criminals hear you.
A metallic container containing tasty paint.
Used to remove color from anything.
A crafting bench fitted with tools, securing mechanisms, and a steady surface for blacksmithing.
It's Gerald! The NTR's trustworthy golden frog!
A homemade bar of soap. Smells of... well....
A frame for constructing your own computer. Or console. Whichever name you prefer.
A spring loaded gun designed to fit syringes, used to incapacitate unruly patients from a distance.
A type of plumbing constructor designed to harvest from geysers and collect their fluids.
A mount for trophy fish, to show off your proudest catch.
For Cocktails, Chemistry, and Catastrophe. - The HoochMaster Deluxe.
Barman Recipes: Mixing Drinks and Changing Lives
An adorable stuffed toy that resembles a very determined spacefaring lizardperson. To infinity and beyond, little guy.
Used to retrieve cell lines from organisms. Don't worry, it won't sting.
A figurine depicting a Botanist that surely won't let kudzu get out of control.
A freezer containing packs of blood.

A guide to the drone shell dispenser, detailing the constructive and destructive applications of modern repair drones, as well as the development of the incorruptible cyborg servants of tomorrow, available today.
An embossed piece of paper from the Third University of Harvard.
The input side of a turbine generator, contains the compressor.
A warning sign which reads 'DISPOSAL: LEADS TO ENGINE'.
A faint aura of unease and asspainery surrounds the bottle.
A locked box used to store medals of honor.
It would seem it vends dyes, and other stuff to make you pretty.
A remote control switch for a mechanical curtain.
A pipe, for smoking. Probably made of meerschaum or something.
